analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is unsafe length use when comparing/copying parsed tuple strings: code uses attacker-controlled parsed lengths (`value_siz` / `val2.value_size`) as the `n` argument to `strncmp`/`strncpy` without proving the referenced source buffer is that large and valid for string reads. In particular, after `dissect_softether_type(VALUE_DATA, &val1, ...)`, it does `strncmp(val1.value.ptr.value_str, "host_name", value_siz)`, where `value_siz` is the total consumed field size (metadata + payload), not the actual string length. Similar pattern exists for `ddns_fqdn` check and subsequent `strncpy` from parsed pointers. This causes over-read from poisoned bytes (ASan use-after-poison) in `strncpy` at line ~223.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered via `fuzz_process_packet` -> `ndpi_detection_process_packet` -> `ndpi_search_softether`, when packet payload length is >=99 so SoftEther host/FQDN parser runs. A crafted SoftEther-like payload must make tuple parsing succeed enough to set `got_fqdn`/`got_hostname` and provide VALUE_STR/VALUE_DATA entries whose reported sizes/consumed sizes are inconsistent with actual accessible bytes, so `strncmp`/`strncpy` read past valid packet data into poisoned redzone. Input is fully attacker-controlled packet bytes from the harness.
